primary_question: Can the automatic audit identify actual defects in a fixed preliminary score without confusing already-accounted reply defects with new scoring failures?
comparison: Apply old reply-only trigger and new score-aware trigger to the SAME new audit output; not two randomized model arms or a causal attribution to score links alone.
intervention: Explicit score links plus delivery of the unchanged complete frozen rubric, absent from the earlier audit input. No new q/m anchors.

repeats: V3_OFF and dev06B each twice with independent repetition/request IDs; repeats are not new cases; no post-result sampling.
reporting: old/new trigger difference on same output
numeric_policy: No new q/m/U scores or repairs in this batch; do not infer corrected ON/OFF gains. Historical numbers remain unchanged.
advancement: If both06B readings locate the specific unsupported action and its missing/misclassified preliminary assessment, and V3_OFF repeats recognize prior accounting without invented omissions, and controls show no new clearly source-disproved finding, this supports a local automated-linkage mechanism. A justified severity/q concern in V3_OFF is not automatically a failure or redundant repair. No reward qualification.
negative_exit: Failure to locate the known score defect or repeated fabricated score accusations rejects this candidate for automatic routing; inspect existing claim check and scoring rationale, do not add prompts or sample to pass.
uncertainty_exit: Reasoned severity/q ambiguity remains unresolved; disagreement cannot be classified as error without a sufficient reference. Unknown or excessive missingness yields inconclusive, never success by abstention.
technical_exit: First technical/binding/truncation/unknown-usage or liability/budget failure stops; preserve all attempts/reservations, no retry.
human_gap: No new questionnaire needed for this local diagnostic. Exact q/m correctness and independent generalization remain unsupported, so this batch cannot qualify a reward.
